subject: POC next steps & model selection — Acme Retail trial
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lexi Martinez <lexi@acme-retail.com>; Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + next steps — Acme Retail POC (model selection, success criteria, owners)

Hi Lexi / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short post-call recap and proposed plan to kick off the 2-week POC/trial for the storefront search & product Q&A use case. Please review and confirm or flag anything missing.

1) Success criteria (Agreed goal)
- Search relevance improvement: +8–12% MRR (proxy metric: increase in add-to-cart rate from search results for flagged queries)
- Avg answer latency under 350ms (95th percentile) for user-facing Q&A API
- Multilingual support: Spanish & French must match English baseline for top-30 intents (>= 85% relative accuracy)
- No PII leakage in responses; pass our baseline prompt safety checks

2) Evaluation plan & metrics
- We'll provide a labeled evaluation set (2k queries across EN/ES/FR). Redwood will run automated evals and share precision/recall + example failures.
- On the integration side, we'll run a 3-day shadow traffic run to measure latency and cache-hit improvement.

3) Model selection (recommended for trial)
- Primary model: Mistral-7B-Instruct (open, performant for instruction tasks and multilingual fine-tuning)
- Fallback model: Llama2-13B-chat (for edge cases and longer-context Q&A)
- Quantization profile: 4-bit q4_0 for Mistral to hit latency targets; we can run a quick A/B with float16 if quality regresses

4) Timeline & owners
- Week 0 (this week): exchange evaluation set + IAM access for Redwood to test (owner: Lexi / Carlos)
- Week 1: Build integration + run automated evals (owner: Ben Carter)
- Week 2: Shadow traffic + results review; final recommendation (owner: Marissa Cole)

5) Next steps (action items)
- Lexi: share evaluation dataset and a sample of traffic logs (pseudonymized) by Fri 2/20
- Carlos: grant read-only S3 access and a short runbook for auth (by 2/20)
- Ben: spin up trial config, run model vs fallback comparison, and share initial numbers by Mon 2/23

Attachments: I attached a short POC success-criteria doc and a model comparison CSV (stub) to make review easier.

If that looks good I'll schedule a quick sync for Mon to align on implementation details.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Acme Retail POC (model selection, success criteria, owners)

Thanks Marissa — this is great, and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications:

- Evaluation set: we'll send the labeled set (EN/ES/FR) by end of day Fri (2/20). We have about ~1.8k labeled queries and will add 200 more Spanish examples.
- Latency: 350ms 95th is ambitious but reasonable. For our internal dashboards, we currently see 95th at ~420ms for our baseline search when we enrich results. If Redwood can get us below 350ms in shadow that would be a big win.
- Security: we'll expect SOC2 evidence and a short data handling summary before any production traffic.

One note on models: our infra lead prefers starting with Llama2-13B-chat as the first baseline because we've previously benchmarked it internally (easier for our SRE to reason about memory/throughput). We're okay trying Mistral-7B-Instruct as primary if Redwood can provide the quantization profile and expected throughput numbers.

We'll share S3 sample and dataset by Fri. Scheduling: Mon 2/23 at 11am PT works for a quick sync with Ben.

—Lexi
Lexi Martinez
Director, Product — Search & Recommendations

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps — Acme Retail POC (model selection, success criteria, owners)

Looping in a quick systems note on model selection and perf expectations.

- Throughput/latency: On an A100-ish instance with Redwood runtime and q4_0 quantization, Mistral-7B-Instruct hits ~220–300ms p95 for 512-token context (sampling/greedy) in our internal tests. Llama2-13B-chat at float16 is ~380–450ms p95 on the same hw. Those numbers align with Lexi's expectation to prefer Llama2 initially for predictability; we can present both profiles in the benchmark doc.
- Multilingual: Mistral shows decent zero-shot Spanish/French coverage; for the top-30 intents I'd estimate 80–90% relative accuracy vs EN. Llama2-13B-chat is comparable after light instruction-tuning on translated examples.
- Fallback routing: Recommend a routing policy — primary=Mistral-7B, fallback=Llama2-13B-chat. If latency SLO is violated on Mistral for a particular request, route to Llama2 (configurable in Redwood Console).

I'll prepare an initial model_perf.csv and a short quantization note for Mon's sync. Ben (owner for integration) will stand up the trial infra and run the A/B.

—Ben
